name: Embroidered
intro: Give your design a stitched finish with visible thread texture. Explore embroidered patches for your brand, team or business.
heading: Let the stitching shape the design.
body: The finished size, lettering and small details matter when artwork is translated into stitches. Include your intended dimensions and the item the patch will be used on.
consider: Artwork with clear shapes, lettering and areas of color. Final suitability depends on size and detail.
question: Will small lettering work?
answer: Include the lettering and intended patch dimensions in your request. Suitability needs to be checked at the final size.

name: Woven
desc: A flatter surface. A finer feel.
intro: Explore a flatter woven finish for your custom patch design. Start with your artwork and the finished size you have in mind.
heading: Start with the details that matter.
body: If your design includes small lettering or fine lines, highlight them in your request. The final result depends on the artwork, dimensions and production specification.
consider: Designs where a flatter surface and fine-detail approach are part of the brief.
question: How is woven different from embroidered?
answer: Woven patches use interlaced threads to create the design and generally have a flatter surface. Embroidered patches show the texture of stitches over a base. Compare real examples at the intended size.

name: PVC
intro: Explore molded PVC patches with a dimensional look. Start with your design, size and intended use.
heading: Define the shape and the surface.
body: Point out any raised areas or details that are important to your design. Include the item the patch will be attached to and your preferred attachment method, if known.
consider: A dimensional surface, distinct outlines and raised areas that can be reviewed against your artwork.
question: Can my design have raised detail?
answer: Include a reference showing the effect you want. The achievable detail and construction need to be confirmed for your design.

name: Chenille
intro: Explore the soft, textured look of chenille for bold lettering and patch designs. Start with your idea and the item it will be used on.
heading: Make room for the texture.
body: Include the finished size and the garment or accessory you have in mind. Clearly identify any lettering or detail that must stay readable in the finished patch.
consider: Bold letters and shapes where the plush texture is a central part of the design.
question: Can chenille include small text?
answer: Fine details need to be reviewed against the intended size and construction. Share the full design and mark any details that cannot change.

name: Leather
intro: Explore leather patches for branded apparel and accessories. Start with your design, intended size and application.
heading: Start with the material and finish.
body: If you have a particular material, color or surface effect in mind, include a reference. Material composition and the available finish should be confirmed in the quote.
consider: The look of the material, its color and the intended surface effect on apparel, bags or accessories.
question: What material and finish can I choose?
answer: Material composition, color, thickness and available finishes need confirmation for each project. This review site does not establish whether genuine leather, synthetic alternatives or both will be offered.
